RagShortTexts: The standing military of Xionites in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Xionites rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Xionites against overwhelming regional adversaries.

The horn sounds, and the horse archers wheel into a crescent, loosing arrows over the heads of the spearmen. Armored horsemen smash into the front line while the rear files thrust lances through the gaps. A rider who turns his horse from the fight is cut down by his own squadron, since a broken formation on the steppe means death for everyone who rides with him.

The commanders gather on a low rise with a crude map of the steppe scratched into a felt sheet. Victory depends on remounts reaching the wings and grain wagons keeping pace with the army. Once the center holds, the lancers can sweep around the enemy's flank, and the lords who raised the troops will claim their share of the horses and captured herds.
